reproduction_target: Construction of MycoMobilome, a non-redundant fungal transposable-element (TE) consensus database: (a) sourcing 4,309 public fungal genome assemblies + proteomes via Mycotools, (b) per-genome de novo TE library construction with Earl Grey `earlGreyLibconstruct`, (c) MMseqs2 easy-cluster redundancy reduction to the 80-80-80 rule, (d) six-frame translation (EMBOSS transeq) and protein-evidence screening against RefSeq Fungi (Diamond BLASTp), REPET Pfam35.0/GypsyDB HMM profiles (HMMER hmmscan) and RepeatPeps.lib (BLASTp), (e) host-gene and quality filtering (<120bp, >=5% N via seqtk), (f) classification labelling and naming, and (g) a benchmark comparison in which C. neoformans (GCF_000149245.1), M. oryzae (GCF_000002495.2) and C. albicans (SC5314 Assembly 22) are annotated with `earlGreyAnnotationOnly` using MycoMobilome versus each community's existing TE approach, with overlap computed by BEDTools intersect and coverage/Venn figures in R. There is no wet-lab component: all genomes and proteomes are pre-existing public data.
granularity_note: Coarse one-step-per-named-tool/analysis, built from the bioRxiv v2 JATS XML Materials and Methods (fetched successfully; title phrase 'MycoMobilome' verified present in the fetched XML, 5 hits) plus the GitHub landing page/README prose at https://github.com/TobyBaril/MycoMobilome. 16 computational steps, 0 wet-lab steps (W=0). IMPORTANT BOUNDARY CALL on capture_claim: the cited repository is DOI-archived on Zenodo as a tagged GitHub release snapshot (10.5281/zenodo.17473060 = 'TobyBaril/MycoMobilome: MycoMobilome v1.1', a 354 kB zip of the v1.1 tag), which literally matches the 'release_snapshot' enum. However the snapshotted repository root contains only LICENSE, README.md and MycoMobilome_v1.1_consensuslist.md - no .sh/.py/.R/.nf/Snakefile/Dockerfile/environment.yml and no workflow of any kind. The README is user guidance for consuming the database, not the pipeline that built it. Snapshotting a documentation-only repo captures no analysis code, so a Stage-2 code read would yield zero R-star gain; capture_claim is therefore recorded as exact_pins_partial (the real ceiling comes from the partial prose version pins) and stage2_candidate is false. If the orchestrator prefers the literal reading of the enum, this paper flips to release_snapshot / stage2_candidate=true - flagging explicitly rather than deciding silently. Secondary note: the paper's Data Availability cites 10.5281/zenodo.17037468 while the body text and the v2 metadata cite 10.5281/zenodo.17037469 (v1.0 record); the README now distributes MycoMobilome v1.1 from zenodo record 18243921, i.e. the database has moved past the version the Methods describe.

steps.label: Sourcing of all publicly available fungal genomes + proteomes with Mycotools (version 0.32.3), followed by MANUAL filtering to remove embargoed assemblies (4,309 retained)
Per-genome de novo TE library construction: `earlGreyLibconstruct` in Earl Grey (v4.4.0) configured with Dfam curated elements only (v3.7), run over all 4,309 assemblies

Redundancy reduction of the combined 773,843-sequence FASTA with MMseqs2 `easy-cluster` (`--min-seq-id 0.8 -c 0.8 --cov-mode 1 --cluster-reassign`) to 354,315 representatives - MMseqs2 carries NO version
Six-frame translation of every TE consensus with `transeq -clean -frame 6` in EMBOSS (v6.6.0)
Host-protein similarity search against the Fungi partition of RefSeq release 228 using Diamond BLASTp (v2.1.11) with `--sensitive --matrix BLOSUM62 --evalue 1e-3`
TE protein-domain detection with HMMscan in HMMER (v3.4), `-E 10 --noali`, against ProfilesBankForREPET_Pfam35.0_GypsyDB (REPET suite); hits filtered at fseq_evalue <= 0.001 and fseq_bitscore >= 50

TE protein-domain detection with BLASTp (v2.14.1+) against RepeatPeps.lib from RepeatMasker (v4.1.9), min e-value 1e-3, followed by UNSCRIPTED nested-hit removal and combining of adjacent/overlapping hits

Host-gene designation per the two-rule criterion of Zhang et al. 2020 (ref 25): (i) RefSeq hits and no TE hits, or (ii) both, with >=90 residues aligned to RefSeq not overlapping TE alignments; 24,571 consensus sequences removed - criteria stated in prose, no implementation released
Quality filtering: removal of consensus sequences <120 bp and of sequences with >=5% N using `seqtk comp` (seqtk cited only by GitHub URL, NO version); 53,103 sequences removed, 276,642 retained

Automated protein-evidence classification labelling (_PE / _DA / _NE) and assignment of the MycMob1.0_family-... naming scheme to every consensus - scheme described, decision logic and code not released

Baseline C. neoformans annotation: assembly CNA3 H99 (GCF_000149245.1) annotated with RepeatMasker (v4.1.9) configured with Dfam (v3.9) and RepBase RepeatMasker Edition (release 20181026), options `-species fungi -norna -no_is`

Baseline M. oryzae annotation: reference assembly MG8 (GCF_000002495.2) annotated with RepeatMasker using the curated TE library published with Lin et al. 2024 (ref 9) - no RepeatMasker options or library version given for this run

Baseline C. albicans annotation: community feature GFF for SC5314 Assembly 22 downloaded from candidagenome.org and filtered to features named long_terminal_repeat, repeat_region, retrotransposon - no download date, release/version, or checksum for the community resource; filtering not scripted
MycoMobilome annotation of all three assemblies with `earlGreyAnnotationOnly` in Earl Grey (v6.3.2), MycoMobilome supplied as input library, all other settings default
Identification of shared and approach-unique TE hits with BEDTools intersect (v2.31.1) - subcommand and version given, no flags/overlap thresholds stated

Feature-coverage calculation (per-method annotation widths at shared loci) and Venn diagram generation in R (v4.4.3) with tidyverse and ggVennDiagram (both UNPINNED); Figure 1 / Supplementary Table 1 - no script released

headline.static_readiness: 0/16 (0%) - stage1 ceiling only, no R-star (R-star needs stage-2 code verification)
headline.inference_inclusive_upper_bound: RI ceiling on 7/16 computational steps (C2, C4, C5, C6, C11, C14, C15) - all of them steps where a named tool carries an exact prose version pin AND an explicit command/flag string. The other 9/16 cap at NI for two recurring reasons: (a) unpinned tools - MMseqs2, seqtk, tidyverse and ggVennDiagram appear with no version at all (C3, C9, C16); (b) absent code - the host-gene rule application (C8), the BLASTp nested/adjacent hit merging (C7), the quality filtering (C9), the _PE/_DA/_NE labelling and naming scheme (C10), the candidagenome GFF filtering (C13) and the R coverage/Venn analysis (C16) are described in prose only, and the cited repository contains no scripts. Even at stage 2 no step could exceed RI without an executed environment capture: there is no lockfile, no container, and no conda environment specification anywhere in the paper or README (the README's only install line is `mamba install -n earlgrey bioconda::earlgrey`, itself unpinned).
headline.coverage: 16 computational steps assessed from the bioRxiv v2 JATS XML Materials and Methods plus the GitHub landing page/README prose. 0 wet-lab steps (W=0): the study consumes only pre-existing public genome assemblies and proteomes, so there is no out-of-scope physical work.

gaps.where: Analysis code for the entire database-construction pipeline (Data Availability + github.com/TobyBaril/MycoMobilome)
gaps.missing: The repository named in Data Availability contains NO analysis code. Its root holds only LICENSE, README.md and MycoMobilome_v1.1_consensuslist.md; the README is user guidance for consuming the database ('how to best implement the MycoMobilome dataset into TE annotation pipelines') plus contribution instructions. There is no shell/Python/R script, no Nextflow/Snakemake workflow, and no driver that chains C1-C16. Six steps (C7 nested/adjacent hit merging, C8 host-gene rule application, C9 length and N-content filtering, C10 _PE/_DA/_NE labelling and name construction, C13 GFF feature filtering, C16 coverage + Venn analysis) exist only as prose descriptions of custom logic.
gaps.how_to_close: Publish the actual construction pipeline (the per-genome Earl Grey driver, the clustering/filtering scripts, the host-gene rule implementation, the naming/labelling script, and the R analysis that produced Figure 1 and Supplementary Table 1) in the same repository, and archive that code-bearing commit to Zenodo.

gaps.where: Software environment for all 16 steps (Methods + README)
gaps.missing: No environment lockfile, no container image or digest, and no conda/mamba environment specification is claimed anywhere. Versions are given inline in Methods prose only. The README's single install instruction, `mamba install -n earlgrey bioconda::earlgrey`, has no version constraint and therefore resolves to whatever Bioconda serves at install time - a floating environment for the very tool the recommended workflow depends on.
gaps.how_to_close: Ship a conda-lock/pixi lockfile or a container digest that pins the full closure (Earl Grey 4.4.0 and 6.3.2, RepeatMasker 4.1.9, HMMER 3.4, Diamond 2.1.11, BLAST+ 2.14.1, EMBOSS 6.6.0, MMseqs2, seqtk, BEDTools 2.31.1, R 4.4.3 + tidyverse + ggVennDiagram), and pin the Bioconda install line to an exact build.

gaps.where: C3 (MMseqs2), C9 (seqtk), C16 (tidyverse, ggVennDiagram); plus a paper-vs-README discrepancy on RepeatMasker
gaps.missing: Four tools carry no version identifier of any kind: MMseqs2 (the clustering step that defines the entire non-redundant set), seqtk (cited only by its GitHub URL), tidyverse and ggVennDiagram. Separately, the Methods pin RepeatMasker at v4.1.9 while the GitHub README lists 'RepeatMasker v4.1.5 and v4.1.9 reference databases', so the RepeatMasker/RepeatPeps provenance differs between the two sources the paper directs readers to.
gaps.how_to_close: Add exact version strings for MMseqs2, seqtk, tidyverse and ggVennDiagram in Methods, and reconcile the RepeatMasker version between the manuscript and the README (state which version supplied RepeatPeps.lib for C7 and which ran the C11/C12 annotations).

gaps.where: C1 (Mycotools sourcing + manual embargo filtering), C12 (M. oryzae RepeatMasker run), C15 (BEDTools intersect), C16 (coverage computation)
gaps.missing: Parameters are absent for four steps: no Mycotools command, query date, or embargo-filter criterion is given for the retrieval that produced the 4,309-assembly set; the M. oryzae RepeatMasker run states neither options nor the version/accession of the ref-9 TE library; BEDTools intersect is named without flags or overlap thresholds (so -f/-r/-wo choices are unknown, and these change the shared-versus-unique base-pair counts in Figure 1); and the R coverage/width calculation at shared loci is described narratively with no parameters.
gaps.how_to_close: Record the exact command lines (including the Mycotools query date and the embargo filter rule) and the BEDTools intersect flags, and state the M. oryzae RepeatMasker invocation and input library version.

gaps.where: External resources consumed by C11 and C13
gaps.missing: RepBase RepeatMasker Edition (release 20181026), required to reproduce the C. neoformans baseline, is a subscription/licence-restricted resource and is not freely redistributable - this is the only non-public data dependency in the study (data axis scored 1 for C11). The C. albicans community annotation is retrieved from a bare candidagenome.org download path with no release date, snapshot version, or checksum, so the GFF served in the future need not equal the GFF used.
gaps.how_to_close: State the licence route and exact RepBase release used (already given) and note it is access-restricted; deposit or checksum the specific C. albicans Assembly 22 GFF snapshot that was filtered, or cite it via a versioned CGD release identifier.

gaps.where: Intermediate artifacts of the construction pipeline (Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.17037469)
gaps.missing: Only the final products are deposited (three FASTA libraries, the 4,309-assembly metadata xlsx, two protein-hit tables, README; 471.6 MB, CC-BY-4.0, v1.0, verified live). Not deposited: the 4,309 per-genome de novo Earl Grey libraries, the combined 773,843-sequence FASTA, the MMseqs2 cluster assignments, the 24,571 host-gene-flagged and 53,103 quality-failed sequences that were removed, and the per-genome TE annotation GFFs for the three benchmark assemblies. Reproducing any intermediate count therefore requires re-running the entire 4,309-genome pipeline.
gaps.how_to_close: Deposit the intermediate FASTAs, the cluster membership table, and the removed-sequence lists, plus the six benchmark annotation GFFs (three MycoMobilome, three baseline) that Figure 1 is computed from.

gaps.where: Repository snapshot / version alignment between paper, Zenodo, and README
gaps.missing: The repository is GPL-3.0 licensed and IS archived as a tagged release snapshot (10.5281/zenodo.17473060 = 'TobyBaril/MycoMobilome: MycoMobilome v1.1', 354 kB zip of tag v1.1) - but the snapshot contains documentation only, so it is a citable artifact without a reproducible one inside. Three version/DOI inconsistencies also exist: Data Availability cites 10.5281/zenodo.17037468 while the body text and article metadata cite 10.5281/zenodo.17037469; the Zenodo v1.0 record is flagged 'a newer version of the record available'; and the README now distributes MycoMobilome v1.1 from zenodo record 18243921, i.e. the released database has moved past the v1.0 the Methods describe, with no changelog in the manuscript.
gaps.how_to_close: Point the DOI in Data Availability at the specific record version used in the Methods (or state the concept-DOI/version-DOI relationship explicitly), add a database changelog mapping v1.0 to v1.1, and archive a code-bearing release rather than a documentation-only one.

gaps.missing: 'Genomes were manually filtered to remove those under embargo, resulting in a final set of 4,309 genome assemblies.' The filtering is a human decision applied to a moving upstream resource; while the resulting assembly list is deposited (assemblyRecord.xlsx), the decision rule and the pre-filter candidate set are not, so the step is replayable only by accepting the authors' output list, not by re-deriving it.
gaps.how_to_close: Record the Mycotools query date, the pre-filter assembly list, and the machine-checkable embargo criterion so the 4,309-assembly set can be re-derived rather than merely re-used.
